summary.oneLiner: GAVL crossed INR 10,000 Cr revenue with 9% growth driven by volume-led expansion in Animal Nutrition and Oil Palm, while Crop Care faces a temporary inventory overhang before a projected H2 recovery. The strategic pivot to high-value segments (branded foods, specialty agrochemicals) and Astec's EBITDA breakeven mark a inflection in earnings quality, supported by a 'demographic dividend' in oil palm plantations offsetting near-term monsoon risks.
summary.business: Godrej Agrovet makes and sells animal nutrition products (cattle feed, layer feed, aqua feed and specialty nutrition), crop protection products (in-house differentiated herbicide and insecticide formulations plus selectively in-licensed products) and oil palm products (crude palm oil, palm kernel oil and allied products processed from Fresh Fruit Bunches), selling primarily to Indian farmers through deep on-ground farmer engagement, field demonstrations and advisory networks. Through its subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates the Company also has interests in dairy products, poultry, value-added vegetarian and non-vegetarian products, cattle breeding and dairy farming, and — via Astec LifeSciences — agrochemical active ingredients (technical), bulk and formulations and intermediate products, including a contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) business. Its footprint extends beyond India through the ACI Godrej Agrovet joint venture in Bangladesh, Astec's exports to approximately 17 countries, and an Astec subsidiary in Bogota, Colombia.

Animal Nutrition: Dhanalaxmi G (premium cattle feed for high-yielding cows and buffaloes, launched FY 2025-26)
Bypro Plus (enhanced protein formulation, launched FY 2025-26)
Vegetable Oil / Oil Palm: Fresh Fruit Bunch (FFB) procurement and milling
Oil palm plantation development and nursery operations

20,000+ farmers supported through CSR initiatives|Brand equity in Animal Nutrition - repeatedly cited 'strong brand equity' plus the established Bypro franchise and the Dhanalaxmi cattle-feed line, supporting volume-led growth and premium launches|Dedicated R&D infrastructure across segments - NGCARD (Nashik) for cattle/broiler/layer feed, the Aqua Feed R&D Centre (Hanuman Junction), the Adi Godrej Centre for Chemical Research & Development (Rabale), plus oil palm R&D; enables customised nutrition products, molecule development in Crop Care/Astec and yield improvements in Oil Palm|Vertically integrated oil palm model - plantation development, nursery operations, FFB procurement, milling with improving oil extraction ratio, and downstream optimisation, giving upstream-to-downstream operating leverage on a maturing asset base|Improving capital efficiency and balance-sheet quality - ROCE improved from 16% in FY 2024-25 to 20% in FY 2025-26 and average working capital days cut from 39 to 25; Board of 12 directors with half independent and 6 women directors (4 of them independent)|Sustainability credentials that are ahead of sector norms - CDP 'A-' leadership band for Climate and Forests for a second consecutive year, water-positive status at ~14x conservation, 78% renewable energy share, and approved science-based emission targets aligned to 'Well Below 2 degrees C'

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 expansion activity at Godrej Agrovet was concentrated in Oil Palm value-chain investment, a feed-plant product conversion and better utilisation of subsidiary capacity, rather than in any newly announced greenfield plant with a commissioning date. In Vegetable Oil, the Directors' Report describes the year's performance as underpinned by "sustained investments across the value chain, including plantation development, nursery operations and deep farmer engagement, with continued focus on scientific agronomy, productivity enhancement and process efficiencies improving yields and mill performance"; the Chairman adds that "continued investments in area expansion, farmer partnerships, and downstream integration have further strengthened our leadership position". The farmer-facing footprint was widened through "the expansion of the Samadhan Center network to 24 Centers during the year". In Animal Nutrition, "Aqua feed production has successfully commenced at the Bani unit, originally designed for poultry feed manufacturing" — the switch was achieved by leveraging the existing layout and infrastructure through in-house process optimisation, parameter tuning and Kaizens, with "Plant utilization increased by up to 14%" and savings of approximately Rs 70 lakh in FY 2025-26. Supporting plant-level technology work during the year included an automatic water recovery system in the boiler circuit (recovery and reuse of more than 750 KL of water per month), temperature sensors and alarm systems on the Crumblers for product-quality control, and implementation of the YKL Press to recover residual oil from Empty Fruit Bunches while lowering their moisture so the processed EFB can be used as boiler fuel (cost savings of approximately Rs 95 lakh). An imported pulverizer installed at a plant for fine grinding of raw material for producing aquaculture feeds (year of import 2023-24) is reported as fully absorbed. The Company states that "the capital expenditure on specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes made by your Company during the Financial Year 2025-26 was Rs 4.53 Crore". At subsidiary Astec LifeSciences, the turnaround to EBITDA break-even was attributed to higher volumes across the enterprise and CDMO portfolios with "enhanced capacity utilization compared to the previous year", and the parent raised its holding from 64.75% to 67.03% by subscribing to Astec's Rights Issue. In Crop Care, expansion was product/crop-led rather than asset-led: new herbicide and insecticide launches (Ashitaka in maize, Takai in paddy) marked "a strategic broadening of crop coverage beyond traditional focus areas". The routed text contains no installed-capacity table, no named plant commissioning or ramp-up timeline, and no forward capex programme or budget.
currentContext.mdna: India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 estimated at 7.6 percent versus 7.1 percent in FY25 (RBI annual report), with the IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook projecting 6.5 percent for both FY27 and FY28 — India retaining its position as the fastest-growing major economy.|Agriculture and allied sector as a stable anchor: real GVA from agriculture and allied activities estimated to grow ~3.1% in FY 2025-26, with moderation attributed to muted food price inflation rather than a decline in physical output.|Strong rural demand indicators — adequate monsoon, healthy reservoir levels, and tractor sales (a key proxy for rural sentiment) up 19 percent in FY26 crossing one million units, reflecting improved farm liquidity and mechanisation.|Key near-term monitorable: the initial long-range forecast for the 2026 southwest monsoon indicates a below-normal rainfall outlook, raising downside risks to kharif sowing and rural sentiment.|Supportive policy backdrop from Union Budget 2026-27 — transition from subsistence to high-value market-linked agri-food systems, integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, high-value crop programmes, fisheries value-chain support, a loan-linked capital subsidy scheme in animal husbandry, and the Bharat VISTAAR AI-enabled advisory platform — expected to create scalable growth opportunities across the value chain for integrated agri-business groups.|Structural transformation of Indian agriculture through precision agriculture, IoT sensors, drones, satellite crop monitoring, AI-driven advisory and digital supply chains, plus growth in agri-tech, agri-fintech and organised agri-logistics.|Animal Nutrition: volume-led growth across cattle, layer, aqua and specialty feed driven by deep farmer engagement, strong brand equity and improving product mix; profitability aided by moderation in key raw material prices, better product mix and continued operational efficiencies.|ACI GAVL (Bangladesh JV): with the conclusion of elections the operating environment is expected to normalize, providing greater stability and improved visibility; long-term outlook positive on structural growth in the livestock sector, increasing formalization of feed consumption and rising acceptance of high-quality performance-oriented nutrition solutions.|Crop Care: near-term demand impacted by adverse weather, acreage shifts and heightened competitive and regulatory intensity in cotton, chilies and grapes; recovery expected to be driven by innovation-led portfolio expansion, increased R&D investment, strategic collaborations and deeper penetration across a wider range of crops and use-cases.|Astec LifeSciences: turnaround supported by higher volumes across enterprise and CDMO portfolios, improved realizations, better demand conditions, enhanced capacity utilization, normalization of channel inventories and improved operating leverage — positioning the company for sustained recovery.|Oil Palm: higher Fresh Fruit Bunch arrivals, sustained improvement in oil extraction ratio, effective cost management and supportive realizations for crude palm oil and palm kernel oil driving revenue and profitability.|Dairy: headwinds from elevated milk procurement costs and temporary demand disruption caused by unseasonal rainfall in the first half of the financial year.|External risk overlay: the ongoing West Asia conflict introduces risks through energy prices, shipping costs and financial market volatility; as a large net importer of crude oil India remains exposed to supply disruptions and price spikes, though strong domestic demand provides a counterbalance. The World Bank projects a slowdown in global growth (~2.5%).|Astec LifeSciences intends to expand its pipeline of complex and differentiated molecules in the CDMO business, leveraging the Adi Godrej Centre for Chemical Research and Development to deepen customer partnerships and support R&D-led scale-up (qualitative pipeline reference; no order-book value disclosed).|Animal Nutrition strengthened its innovation pipeline during the year with the launch of Dhanalaxmi G (premium cattle feed for high-yielding cows and buffaloes) and Bypro Plus (enhanced protein formulation), both seeing encouraging early adoption in initial launch markets.

risks.risk: Climate change and increasing weather volatility
risks.note: Flagged as a key long-term risk for agri-linked businesses. Increasing frequency of unseasonal rainfall, heat stress, droughts, floods and shifting monsoon patterns can materially impact crop acreage, animal productivity, feed availability and demand cycles, affecting volumes, raw material availability, cost structures and farmer purchasing behaviour across multiple verticals. Already realised in FY 2025-26 — unseasonal rain during Q1 disrupted Dairy demand patterns.

risks.risk: Geo-political developments and supply chain disruption
risks.note: Global geo-political tensions, trade disruptions and regional instability pose risks of supply chain interruptions, increased freight costs, commodity price volatility, foreign exchange fluctuations and constrained availability of key inputs such as grains, oilseeds, energy and agrochemical raw materials. The Company diversifies sourcing and optimises inventories, but prolonged disruptions could impact input costs and margins.

risks.risk: Raw material availability, price volatility and supplier dependency
risks.note: Businesses depend on availability of quality raw materials at competitive prices. Prices of maize, soya, oilcakes, milk, energy, packaging materials and chemical intermediates are volatile, driven by weather, global demand-supply, currency, trade policies and regulatory changes. Dependence on third-party suppliers and logistics partners adds exposure to supply disruptions, cost escalation and delivery delays.

risks.risk: Regulatory, policy and compliance risk across agri, food and agrochemicals
risks.note: Sectors are subject to evolving oversight on product approvals, pricing controls, environmental norms, sustainability disclosures, product safety, labelling and quality standards. Changes in frameworks, approval delays or restrictive policy actions may impact product launches, cost structures and business continuity; rising ESG expectations require continuous investment in compliance, sustainability and reporting systems.

risks.risk: Capital allocation, execution and people risk in a diversified multi-vertical structure
risks.note: Managing diversified operations across multiple geographies and business verticals requires strong execution discipline, leadership depth and robust internal controls. Risks around talent availability, succession planning, digital capability absorption, project execution and integration of new initiatives may impact long-term value creation if not managed effectively. Leadership transition was live during the year — the Managing Director superannuated with effect from close of business on August 31, 2025, with a CEO & Managing Director appointed to the Managing Committee from September 1, 2025.

risks.risk: Milk procurement cost inflation and competitive intensity in the Dairy business
risks.note: The Dairy business faced a significantly challenging operating environment in FY 2025-26; sustained inflation in milk procurement prices exerted meaningful pressure on margins and heightened competitive intensity in certain markets weighed on financial performance. Mitigation is via cost control, operating efficiencies, portfolio optimisation and a brand-led / value-added strategy, but recovery is explicitly conditioned on input cost pressures moderating.

risks.risk: Feed cost volatility and pricing pressure in Poultry & Processed Foods
risks.note: The business operates in a dynamic environment characterised by feed cost volatility and pricing pressures; profitability remained influenced by fluctuations in input costs and competitive intensity. Margin improvement is dependent on input cost volatility moderating and operating leverage improving.

risks.risk: Pan-India operating exposure to economic, regulatory and political conditions and competitor actions
risks.note: The Board's Report states the Company has substantial operations spread almost all over the country and its competitive position is influenced by economic, regulatory and political situations and the actions of competitors. The Board, supported by the Audit Committee, reviews the effectiveness of the risk management process covering all material risks; the Board's stated opinion is that no risks have been identified which may threaten the existence of the Company. Risk Management Committee met twice in FY 2025-26 (August 6, 2025 and February 3, 2026).

one-line thesis: GAVL crossed INR 10,000 Cr revenue with 9% growth driven by volume-led expansion in Animal Nutrition and Oil Palm, while Crop Care faces a temporary inventory overhang before a projected H2 recovery. The strategic pivot to high-value segments (branded foods, specialty agrochemicals) and Astec's EBITDA breakeven mark a inflection in earnings quality, supported by a 'demographic dividend' in oil palm plantations offsetting near-term monsoon risks.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,333 Cr (Q4, +9% YoY); FY26: INR 10,233 Cr (+9% YoY). EBITDA/PBT: Q4 PBT (ex-exceptional) INR 87 Cr (+16.8% YoY); FY26 PBT (ex-exceptional) INR 569 Cr (+17.2% YoY). PAT: Not explicitly broken out, driven by margin expansion. Order Book: N/A (FMCG/Agri flow business). Net Debt: Working capital reduction noted; FY27 free cash surplus est. INR 100-125 Cr post-capex. One-offs: INR 9.5 Cr profit from pet food contract manufacturing booked under 'Other Income' rather than revenue, distorting segment margin visibility.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Early double-digit for consolidated FY27; Animal Nutrition, Oil Palm, Branded Foods targeting double-digit volume growth. Crop Care targeting 'high double-digit' recovery from Q2 onwards. Margins: Mid-teens PBT growth targeted; Milk procurement costs expected to normalize from Q2 FY27. Capex: INR 350-400 Cr for FY27 (75-80% growth capex; ~50% allocated to Oil Palm).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for this business model; focus on volume throughput and plantation yield cycles.
segment / subsidiary detail: Animal Nutrition: Q4 volumes +15% YoY (Cattle feed +24%); driven by new products (Dhanlaxmi, Bypro Plus) and shift from unbranded due to high milk prices. Oil Palm: Record area expansion; all-time high oil extraction ratio; Q4 seasonally weak but margins resilient. Crop Care: Q4 impacted by channel inventory carry-forward; recovery expected from Q2 FY27 with new launches (Ashitaka for maize, TAKAI for rice) targeting 16-18% revenue contribution in FY27. Astec LifeSciences: EBITDA breakeven achieved in FY26; CDMO-led growth; 53% revenue from exports. Dairy (Creamline): Revenue +5% (ex-bulk); margins pressured by milk costs; value-added mix ~40%. Foods: Branded salience >80%; Live Bird & Yummiez margins improved.
growth verticals / optionality: Oil Palm 'demographic dividend' (50% trees in juvenile 0-4 year stage becoming productive over next 5 years); Crop Care diversification away from cotton/chili dependency to multi-crop (maize, rice); Astec CDMO pipeline scaling; Pet food backend manufacturing expansion.
margins & cost dynamics: Animal Nutrition margins expanded via R&D cost reconfiguration and product mix. Dairy margins compressed by elevated milk procurement costs (expected to cool Q2 onwards). Oil Palm margins aided by extraction ratios. Astec margins improving with capacity utilization.
capex / expansion: FY27 guidance INR 350-400 Cr; ~50% directed to Oil Palm expansion; remainder to growth initiatives in high-return segments. Maintenance vs Growth split: 20-25% maintenance, 75-80% growth.
capital allocation: Surplus cash generation expected (INR 100-125 Cr post-capex in FY27); focus on high-growth businesses; minority shareholder protection emphasized amid potential Astec structural reviews (no final decision in 2-3 quarters).
risks & watch-items: Monsoon/El Nino variability (predicted below normal, but skewed geographically; South region normal may protect Crop Care); Iran/Middle East conflict impacting crude-palm oil correlation and agrochemical demand; Raw material volatility (milk prices, import costs from China for Astec).
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; emphasizing 'volume-led' growth, 'demographic dividend' in plantations, and successful turnaround execution; cautious on external variables (war, monsoon) but bullish on internal levers.
non-obvious takeaways: Pet food manufacturing contributes ~INR 9.5 Cr profit booked as 'Other Income' (not revenue), creating an accounting distortion that understates top-line but boosts bottom-line. Oil Palm business has a 'demographic dividend' where 50% of trees are currently juvenile, promising automatic volume step-up over 5 years regardless of new planting. Crop Care recovery is mathematically guaranteed from Q2 due to base effect of channel inventory destocking in Q1.

themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.
